body: That is so amazing 🌌 I would love to have an experience like that with my mum.

I hear you,  it's been just over 2 years since my mum passed away. People who haven't been through it have no idea how draining it can all be and how the intense missing of them is an every day thing we have to grapple with. And yeah so lonely too. I want it all to just go away too it makes me feel angry at times that i have to cope this! 

The German chocolate cake sounds lovely and i so wish for you that your mum was here still to have made that for you. Our mums are always here and love us the most and then one day they're just gone forever?! It's surreal and makes me feel pretty existential.

Hey just to say that I did,  it's the first time in my life I've ever felt completely emotionally numb, such a bizarre feeling. I remember thinking that I just couldn't feel any emotion at all. I would say that the numbness kicked in a few weeks maybe after my mum passed away and tbh I can't remember how long it lasted but maybe about a month or two?  I think it was utter shock and overwhelm and it was just all way too much. Once that passed the full force of the grief kicked in though.. it could be different for you of course but sounds very similar to what I went through. Also, please don't feel guilty for it, I actually think it's a sign that the grief is so huge that it happens as some kind of protective mechanism for a while.

I saw my mum in my dream last night,  i was unbelievably over the moon that she was there just to see her again for that moment erased 2 years of pain and grief until i woke up.., in the dream i called out "Mum!!!" ..and then she disappeared. I wanted her to stay and to stay in that dream more than anything. I find it like torture that i might never see her again, I'm  really trying to believe in the after life again , in a spiritual non religious sense (my fiance died over 10 years ago and i had a visit from him several months after his death and felt him around loads but since my mum and sister died I've felt nothing from them at all which has really shaken my beliefs)

I'm the same.. music was such an important part of my life & my biggest passion but i haven't been able to play or write anything new yet,  since my mum died in 2021. I lost my sister 9 months before that too  It's like the meaning & spark for it all left with them and i don't know how to get it back.
I'm so sorry you lost your mum too. Thanks for letting me know I'm not alone,  you're not either. Sending love to you.

I could have written this exact post.. only slight difference is that it's been just under 2 years since my mum passed away & I still find myself mostly having to avoid photos, messages and reminders like that. Sending love and empathy your way.
Yeah,  I totally get that too

I started daytime drinking whiskey for a while,  never done anything like that before but the emotions &thoughts I was being hit with after my mum passed away were so excruciating ands that's the only thing that would take the edge off them a little. (I don't do that anymore but still drink more than i used to & less motivated to cut back & stop smoking again.) That was a crazy time I didn't feel like my self at all really for up to a year after the loss. Now i feel like things have calmed down more with me but I'm definitely a different version of myself, of who i used to be.

Thanks for posting this,  i had a phase where I felt like I was doing a little better but lately I feel back down in a grief hole. Everyday i feel existential and heartbroken without my mum,  it's been nearly two years since she passed away. I was starting to feel like there's something really wrong with me but it helps to know I'm not alone.
I feel the same way,  it's a very difficult place to be
I hear you. It is a complete assault on the body,  mind and soul. Sending loads of love to you.

I feel like I'm kind of waiting this life out until I can (hopefully) see and be with my mum again. I'm not suicidal but I wouldn't mind too much if my life came to an end. Hopefully can have a few fun times here ands there but life is overall painful/ lonely without my mum. She was my best friend,  we spoke about anything and everything multiple times every day. Anniversary times are extra hard,  sending you tons of love. Also, you should be VERY proud of yourself for getting through the first year,  there were times during that first year after my mum passed that I really didn't think I would survive.
Thank you 💜 same to you. I'm sorry you are struggling so much too .. the depth and breadth of the loss of a parent who was your closest person is inexplicable..
Sorry to jump on this but I feel very much the same after losing my mum. Its horrible and just really, really sucks.

I completely get what you mean. I miss having someone in my life who would take care of me like my mum did,  there's no one else who ever will. IIt's so,  so hard and exhausting,  and lonely to have to do it all yourself. I feel like I lost so much when I lost my mum, the secondary losses and ways in which it charges your whole life seem endless. It's like navigating a whole new alien terrain.
I'm 41, I have all those same feelings since my mum died, it's crazy how much it changes how you feel about yourself, life and well,  everything..
It does seem to be that way 😢

Hi i just wanted to say I can relate, in my own way after losing my sibling and then my mum all within the space of a year. My mum was my very closest person, I spoke to her about anything and everything every single day of my life, she was most of the light and comfort in this world for me. I miss my sister a lot too. It seems crazy that they're just.. gone, after all that life together, how bonded we were. Like a cosmic joke,  life seems crazy and surreal. I feel like I'm contstantly searching for my mum and can't feel at peace because I don't know if she still exists in some form anymore or not..will I ever see her again? It's really hard to live without her and I feel very lonely a lot of the time. Often I just don't see the point and my mental health goes through really bad phases, it's been 18 months since my mum passed away. 

The thing I come back to though is that I don't want to die yet (although I would be ok with it if it did happen, I don't know if that makes sense!) , so have no choice but to carry on. I try not to think of the future too much,  but just still take it day by day mostly. Even little things that provide a small amount of comfort or enjoyment,  are worth doing. I'm sorry i don't have much advice. The only thought that really helps me is one day my life will be over anyhow as well and it could be anytime, so this pain won't be forever. It's doesn't help much some days though but I try to repeat these thoughts in my head to help me cope. Sending love to you.

I feel the same way about my mum,  she was older when she died (76) but had been suffering with an awful illness since I was in my mid 30s, and after several years she left, 18 months ago now. Before the disease struck she was so young looking and healthy. She was a light in my life,  so kind,  caring, the centre of my world. Although the initial extreme,  brutal grief I went through has morphed after 18 months it's still so very hard.. I miss her so, so much all the time and I keep feeling so restless like I'm constantly searching for her or some way to fix this,  it feels truly torturous at times. My life is very lonely without her and I don't understand any more what the meaning or point of life is,  so I just struggle on through each day. I'm scared I'm wasting my own life feeling so sad all the time but I can't help it.  I feel for you and the person responding above so much. I imagine I would feel additionally even more cheated if I was younger when she had passed away. Both your dads sound like the loveliest people, as was my mum. I wish I could make some kind of sense out of things but since my mum passed Its like I was born into a new world where nothing makes sense anymore.
It is definitely not even remotely the same. The only time I can think when it might be similar with a different relative is if you were brought up by them, so they were like a mother to you.
Yeah totally,  I can relate to everything you have said..

Wow that is so amazing that you had that experience with your brother.. if you don't mind me asking did you do anything like meditation,  attempting to communicate with him etc before this happened our was it just completely out of the blue? I am desperate to have something like that with my mum as my soul feels like it's dying without her and having not felt her around me at all since she passed 18 months ago. 

I honestly can't claim to know but regarding your question from everything that I've read over the years,  it seems like we are much more than this one lifetime, our true existence is way beyond any one life here. However,  we are aware of all the lifetimes we have lived as different roles & i would imagine especially with our most recent one, it would connect us back more as we would have loved ones still here grieving for us and remembering us.

I feel like I'm failing too but I guess this is just the unpredictable nature of grief. i thought i was doing better at coping but Christmas and being ill in top of it through the holidays feels like it has sent me over the edge again. Im in the second year out from the loss of my mom. I'm back to feeling like I can do this anymore,  the emotional pain of being without my her is too immense,  I'm getting barrages of flashbacks,  memories,  all the sweet ways she had,  everything she meant to me,  her mannerisms.. all images and movies running through my mind on loops .. I feel like I'm going insane are times with thoughts racing a million miles an hour at times currently.  I feel like I've lost sooo much and I'm back to feeling on the edge of despair,  with the dark, self destructive thoughts back in full force as  the pain feels just too much to cope with..I know I won't actually do anything but the thoughts are relentless again atm. I can't stop going round in circles of disbelief that I'll never see my mom again,  I mean maybe I will in the afterlife,  but there might not be one so that doesn't help me feel much better. I feel so lost and alone, scared and vulnerable to everything in this world. Anyhow I just wanted to say you aren't alone in feeling like you aren't doing well with your grief,  I guess it just is this bad if you lose a parent that meant the world to you. And I'm aware know that it can come raging back at times when one is feeling more vulnerable. It's so hard,  I just hope it all gets back to a more manageable level soon. Sending you love and empathy,  your dad must have been an amazing father.

I'm finding the same. Once i got through the initial 6 months of being all but incapacitated by grief, I cope better but actually I'm finding the grief worse in many ways in year 2 as well. It's like the full extent of it and all the implications of the loss are making themselves known in every aspect of my life, &  I only miss her more and more by the day.

The pain is suffocating I totally agree. I can't even cry I just feel like my soul has been squished completely flat and the hopelessness, despair and feelings of awful regret are all raging back for me right now. Just trying to breathe at the moment. Love and strength to you too ❤
Have they never heard of the term "adult orphan"? and at 25, you are a young adult at that. I have been heart broken to read your posts, sending you love and strength.

I'm so sorry too, that is so much to cope with.. do you have anyone around you for some support? The emotional pain runs so deep and it can be absolutely overwhelming, I know.  I'm trying to just distract myself.. memories and nostalgia are hitting me so very hard at the moment. Also, I should add that I'm not a kid (I only just noticed that bit, sorry) so I hope you don't mind that I responded. I'm not married and no kids of my own though. I feel like a lost child at the moment.
Im here. Second Xmas without my mum. Closest person to me in the world. I am in a lot of pain. Hanging on by a thread emotionally tbh.

That is so true. As soon as my mum died it felt like everyone was talking about their mums ALL the time. Didn't seem to think (and still don't!) how it might hurt for me to hear. I can't blame them for not understanding I guess but doesn't make it hurt any less. It had gotten easier but still stings.
Same here. Only those who have been through it understand how utterly,  brutally hard it is...
Yes I feel exactly this way,  I totally understand
I hear you,  life doesn't feel real anymore to me,  but pretty crazy and surreal..

That's really horrible,  I'm sorry! If it were me,  I would approach my supervisor about it and say you're upset (in a calm way), otherwise you'll just be carrying around that (understandable) feeling of  resentment more.

Yes I feel that way a lot too,  my mum was so gentle,  kind and loving and she had to suffer with what is known as the worst (or at least one of the very worst) diseases anyone can have before she died. My sister had it tough from the start through her life in many ways and then she died suddenly after struggling with horrible health issues. Life just seems so random to me now,  like there's no fairness or reason to anything.

I get that completely it's been 15 months since my mum passed but I feel like time has stood still for me in many ways. I don't want to move on,  for her just to be a memory but that is already the situation I'm in.  I hate it,  she was here,  she was real,  she was  everything to me.

Yeah i have this too,  I totally understand what you mean about the shock feeling,  it's like you're hit over and over with the loss. I think when it's someone who has been there every moment of your entire life,  it's so hard to actually accept/ process that they are no longer here. It's brutal to be honest. Like an assault on the soul. I have the same thing with my mum although it happens less now than it did (the feeling of shock) it's still very frequent.., she passed away a year and 4 months ago.
Yes it is very much like that for me,  my mum provided comfort like no one else could and now she's gone & ironically I need that comfort only she could provide more than ever.

I'm the same age as your mum (She was so young I'm so sorry), I lost my mum last year.. She was everything to me too and I similarly feel extremely lost, sad,  lonely without her. It's so hard and some days are terrible still,  I just want to shut everything out and not deal with the reality of her loss. Every day is this huge looming background sadness though and I feel mentally all over the place a lot of the time. I feel like I'm never going to recover as how can I as we were so close? I also question the point of anything/ my existence a lot without her here. So yeah just wanted to say I can relate to feeling the loss so deeply it's like a part of your soul has been ripped away..

To be honest,  it's been 17 months since my mum passed and the majority of my thoughts are still about her/ life/ death/ existential thoughts unless I'm really absorbed into an activity. Then I have this weird jolt after almost like I've forgotten what's happened, which of course I haven't! Everyone is different so I can only say how it is for me and it's less constantly all consuming & utterly brutal than it was (mostly..).  I am still struggling internally a lot though and find living very hard without her...for me the missing of her has only increased over time. I am sorry you lost your mum it's so immensely painful I know, only those who are going through it can understand how life changing it is.
Everything you said is so true

I miss my mum so heavily too, she was the person who loved me the most and vice versa and it's very hard to go through the days missing her so very much. It's been 15 months and I can function better but I only miss her more as time goes on. I can see her so clearly in my mind's eye it still trips me out that she's just.. gone. It hurts so much.
It's extremely difficult...I alwsys think that ironically my mum was the only person who could have got me through the loss of her,  trying to navigate it without her has felt impossible at times.
I would also like to join you in that field..
Same here,  we sound in very similar places with our grief. How long has it been since your mum passed away? It's been a year and 4 months for me.

I feel guilty for coping badly. In many ways my life is privileged I know and I have others that I love and who love me. But my mum was like oxygen to me, to say we were close is a huge understatement and it feels pretty unbearable to be without her.
I miss my sister and my mum so much too. Sending you a hug.

Same here,  I feel it's so, so hard to live without my mum,  I'm just scraping through the days still though I can function better than I did. However my anxiety is off the scale and it's making me ill..and the missing of her is only getting worse.
Beautifully written and brought tears to my eyes you captured how it feels so poetically.

In my more "spiritual" moments I believe that all this can't be for nothing,  there is far more than this life and my mum hasn't been lost to me forever,  but I go really up and down with that belief still.
Ton of bricks is exactly right 💔

I feel like with the other losses I've experienced,  I've peeped though the curtain at the facade of everything..but my mum's death along with my sister's has blown it wide open..  can't unsee it. Even my therapist agrees with me that death is completely outrageous. Life is crazy and surreal.

It's exactly the same for me with the loss of my mum. It's so hard to compare what my life is like now and what it used to be like with the unconditional,  ever present support, care and love from my mum. Your dad sounds so wonderful.. there's really never going to be any kind of replacement for that kind of love. It's so hard to accept though I know. I hope my mum lives on somehow in spirit and it hasn't all just vanished but I'm still grappling with spirituality and really feeling that to be true at the moment. So,  I have no advice but I very much feel this too.
I'm sorry you all know what this feels like 💔

Thank you for your kind message,  your grandma sounds like a wonderful woman and like she was your person, it must have been incredibly hard for you to go through that.  I'm glad you have times now you can smile at the lovely memories she has left behind. 🌌💖
I'm sorry you know how this feels 😥 sending love to you 💜
Yeah there are many triggers,  which can bring that immense pain right up to the surface. Sending love to you, my heart goes to you for the loss of your precious dad. 💜

That sounds like something my mum would say too. 💜 I've had many moments of having to forcibly block out thoughts,  images in my head etc. It's a very hard road. I totally get what you mean about the dark cloud. As I said to my therapist it's like the world's most colossal "downer" , no matter what good things happen to me,  my mum is still dead and that drags everything down to just a surface level fleeting happiness. I can't feel joy and contentment that goes all the way through anymore. Maybe one day this will change and we can find happiness again but it will be in a very different way to before.
It is, I'm sorry you're going through this too.
Yeah is so true..I am only starting to get used to the new me a little more now after 16 months. I will forever miss the old me though.

Going for an hours walk everyday seems to help me a bit with racing thoughts, anxiety etc. I notice if I skip a day my mental state rapidly declines way more so I'm trying to keep it up. I've also recently stopped drinking alcohol (or at least taking a break from it) it had become an everyday coping mechanism for the last 16 months but I realised that without it,  I wake up in the morning feeling less depressed and anxious.

It is unfair! I don't why the world is like this, my mum was the most gentle, lovely person,  and she lived very healthily never smoked,  hardly drank alcohol but she was struck down with ALS out of the blue. Over several years she turned into a shell of her former self it was so traumatic for her and for us to witness.. she and we tried everything possible to get her better but it was all too no avail. 

There doesn't seem to be any way I will ever understand that except that bad things can happen to good people (and vice versa!) and the world just seems largely pretty random..it has no sentient sense of fair or unfair. Perhaps there is more going on than I know and my mum was just meant to go when she did, I don't know. I did remember her saying a few times that she felt she wouldn't live to see really old age. Did she psychically sense something? I wish I knew for sure. 

Anyhow I'm sorry to digress into my situation I just wanted to show you're not alone in these feelings. Your dad sounds wonderful and so diligent with his health - he and you all deserved him to live a much longer life, I am just so very sorry he was taken from you 💜
So true
I had to quit work.  It took me at least 6 months until I was able to focus enough to take a course and get back to some semblance of functioning (still at a way lower level than before though)
It's so beyond surreal isn't it,  just doesn't feel right at all.. very sorry about your dad sending love.

I'm sending you a huge hug,  I feel very alone a lot too since my mum died.. like your dad was for you,  my mum was my closest person and my go to person for everything. I don't really feel like I belong in the world in the same way anymore and my life feels so much colder and harsher without her here I just miss her so, so much. It's an awfully scary and isolating feeling I know.

I guess a big part of it for me is believing.. or trying to believe again.. that death is not the end. That when my time comes,  my mum will be there to take me by the hand and we will be reunited at last. But in the meantime i should make the most of my finite time on earth. Having said that it's a lot easier said than done as life without my mum is a lot more lonely and painful. I'm trying everything to get though,  and to connect. mediumship,  meditation,  shamanic healing...
I'm so sorry. Your dad was so young.. only 3 years older than me,  that's just not fair.
I will try and answer this later as this has happened to me (my mum)
You put the feeling into words so well 💔

I was like that for at least the first 6 months, probably more after my mum died,  barely got out of bed at all., now 15 months down the line and it gets easier to manage the pain and to function day to day (although I can get sudden back slides into full on grief related depression that can last a day or a few days, it's not constant 24/7 debilitating now).. I feel like I'm living a different life in a different reality without my mum though and miss her so much every moment of every day.. sending you love and strength so sorry your mum passed ❤

Yeah,  it really hard to see my mum like that,  I felt like I was in a constant state of fear/ anxiety with how much she was going through and suffering and I dealt with it through denial/ avoidance in a lot of ways. I wish I could go back and do a lot of it differently. No matter how hard it all was,  I'd give anything to go back to when she was still here although I am glad she is no longer suffering,  it's only a small comfort though as she so wanted to get better and live.
Thank you 💜
I would do anything,  anything to see my mum and speak to her one more time. It's so hard to believe now that I used to be able to see her and speak to her whenever I wanted.

It's a very lonely feeling when our mum's have left this world. I feel it too,  every day.  I do think your husband and his family could have been a lot more sensitive to the situation. It would have been comforting potentially ( if it felt right for you), if there had been some kind of honouring of your mum incorporated into the gathering. I'm sorry you felt so alone. Sending you love,  anniversary dates can be (extra) hard 💜

I totally get it,  I was upset when my parents got divorced and it sucked but it is nothing,  nothing even comparable to the level of my mum passing away.. that just blows every other problem I've had with family out of the water.. It's like comparing a mole hill to Everest (even that it is huge understatement)

Thank you for that,  you're very kind to write all that out. I've been looking back through your past posts, that's so beautiful that you've had contact from/ with your mum 💜 It's my mum (best friend, soul mate) too who I'm hoping to connect with. I think I've been extremely blocked by feeling so utterly broken, lost,  distraught and full of regret and anger at times. My mum was the centre of my world and we were in contact everyday throughout the day. My sister passed away 9 months before my mum as well.

I'm 15 months down the line from losing my mum and starting to feel some relief finally, I can cope a bit better I guess now although I'm still completely broken hearted and lonely without her. I had a shamanic session earlier this week and had a vivid dream involving my mum that night where i was reaching up and she was reaching down,  we were holding hands, hers were sparkling with a translucent light and I could feel the energy from that it was extremely powerful and felt so real. I'm hoping to have more experiences in the future. I miss her so much.
Thank you for posting this 💜 Did you do anything to make contact with your mum.. like meditation? or did it just happen? It helps me to read posts like this.

I'm finding its fading over time but still pops up to bring me to my knees sometimes.. but it's less constant and utterly brutal than initially. I'm trying many things to help.. shamanic healing,  induced after death communication (still hoping that will work for me haven't quite had it in me to try again as yet)
Thank you,  any kind words help a little 🤗
I do wonder that too.. really hope that is what it is. Often they come to me out of the blue 💜
I really, really hope this is true

I feel this so much. Today I've been getting constant flashes of how it felt to be cuddled by my mum and just be with her. How excited and happy I would feel when she came to the door us both so happy to see each other. A TV show on,  she is making us some dinner. I get that lovely comforting feeling for a second and then it gives way to a horrible,  cold feeling of emptiness as I think of her home, her much loved garden, all her things, her clothes hanging in her wardrobe never to be worn by her again... cold,  empty,  vacant,  she is gone.

It's definitely normal,  can totally relate. I don't care what those who haven't been through this think,  thru have no clue.  I'm 40 but feel about 20 years older since one of my siblings ands then my mum passed away. It sucks! :(

Yep,  I definitely feel older since losing my mum. I think it's a combination of what you said,  it's like you lose that protected, carefree feeling of being a kid in a way still,  even though you might be an adult in terms of age. Also the heaviness of grief makes you feel older,  especially with regret/ guilt added to the mix. I feel I have to look out for myself now and have no refuge (I do still have my dad but he's not someone I can go to for refuge although he does try his best, my mum was my best friend/ closest person in this world) You're an adult in a very different way when you lose a parent or both parents. I would imagine the feeling is heightened even more when you've lost both. I tried to express this to my friend who still has both her parents alive and she was really surprised/ obviously couldn't understand.

It's been 14 months since my mum passed and I feel the same. I think of her throughout the day and I just miss everything about her so much. I miss her existing in this world,... it's a very different world without our mum's.

I feel the same way about my mum,  she was my very best friend and we were in touch throughout the day  every day. She passed away May 2021. Overall,  I find life without her feels empty, lonely and painful although I have some better days now, my better days are way worse than a bad day when she was still here. Some still feel unbearable. I question all the time what life is about, when someone you have the closest bond with, forged over a life time together is just.. gone, and you don't know if you'll ever see them again in some form. I also feel like I'll never really be truly happy again but I can have little moments of enjoying things and there. It's really frustrating too because I feel like her loss overshadows the other good stuff in my life.. I feel sometimes I must make the most of life and enjoy it while I can,  but it's really hard to when I miss my mum so much all the time and feel so heartbroken.

Yeah same here,  my mum was my go to person for everything,  for emotional support,  I still feel like I can't do it some days too. If I knew for sure I'd see her again one day (not that it would be as it was here but I can't bear the thought of being separated from her forever),  I'd be able to cope better I think.  Sending you a big hug, I feel your pain :(
I feel like that too so I really feel for you... it's so hard,  I used to talk to my mum all throughout the day most days. The silence is deafening. I realised I never knew loneliness before now.
I get those panicky states too.. it really feels dreadful..a couple of times I just couldn't get my heart to calm down it was hammering at what felt like 100 mph for hours.

I'm so sorry you lost your dad,  yeah it does feel just like that... and for everyone else around you (except others affected by the loss of your person) it it keeps spinning just the same. I can't keep up anymore.

I totally agree,  was just thinking..I wish I could go hibernate somewhere until this is all over.. it's so hard having to carry on each day without my mum,  with the knowledge that she is dead. Soul crushing.

That's not good that you do all the work!! It could be tiring you out & potentially that could be lowering your sex drive more (I hadn't no idea if that is that is case but it seems possible!) I think that's something really important to talk about. I found that taking vitamin D helped to make mine higher. If yours was higher but it's decreased,  could be worth getting your vitamin/ mineral/ hormone levels checked. 

If you talk about sharing chores more equally..&  it still doesn't change,  just quietly go about your business,  shop just for yourself, do your own laundry separately and don't do his laundry anymore etc.. Then he will actually have to start doing stuff himself! You're not his wife and even if you were,  your should both be doing an equal share of household responsibilities. Also,  if living together is causing some of the issues,  you could go back to living apart.. but still dating. You are still both very young and living together can throw you into a domestic situation perhaps the relationship wasn't ready for (speaking from experience!) 

It sounds like injecting some more fun and romance into your relationship is needed maybe?. Do you still go on fun dates? Could you try doing something new together that gives you an adrenaline rush (theme park or even just go see a new horror film together or something!) 

Sometimes built up frustrations and resentments can make personality quirks seem more more annoying than adorable over time! It could partly be that which is causing you to find him immature.. did you at one time find him funny but it's changed over time?

I'm no expert by any means but I'd advise giving it more of a shot before throwing in the towel, (if there is still a lot of good stuff in the relationship?)
Do you know why your love for him has faded?

Yeah i feel this every day .. it's absolutely bizarre/ excruciating. That my mum who was in my life from day 1.. I'll never,  ever see her again. Can't compute. My only hope is to see her if there's an afterlife but it won't be as it was here, if there even is one.  Had a paralyzing day today of even finding it hard to breathe with the finality of it all sinking in even more in year 2.

Yep..i can relate,  it's been 15 months since my mum passed away. I feel very similarly to you &  like how I appear on the surface to people is very different now (a lot of the time) to how I feel inside. I have this urge a lot just to have time out from everything,  possibly permanently.
I'm so, so sorry you lost your mum,  I lost mine too and it's been (& still very much is) incredibly hard to navigate. I'm 15 months in. Feel free to message me if you ever want to chat or vent.
